ZORYVEX — Beyond Orbit. Beyond Limits.
summary: We developed an interactive, data-driven web application that integrates open NASA Earth-observation datasets to monitor and analyze environmental changes in real time. Our solution directly addresses the NASA Space Apps challenge by translating complex satellite telemetry and geospatial data into actionable, easy-to-understand visualizations and automated alerts for everyday users. This project matters because it bridges the gap between raw scientific space data and community-level decision-making. By empowering local stakeholders, researchers, and authorities with timely environmental insights, our platform drives sustainable resource management, improves disaster preparedness, and enhances climate resilience for vulnerable communities
details:
How It Works & Key Benefits:

Our solution is an interactive web platform that fetches, processes, and visualizes open NASA Earth-observation datasets in real time. By converting raw satellite telemetry and geospatial layers into intuitive maps, charts, and automated alerts, users can easily monitor environmental indicators without needing advanced data-science skills.

Intended Impact:

The project empowers local communities, researchers, and decision-makers with actionable, timely insights to support sustainable resource management, improve early disaster preparedness, and strengthen climate resilience.

Tools, Technologies & Software Used:

We built the data processing and analysis pipeline using Python (Pandas, NumPy, and geospatial libraries) alongside Google Colab, and developed the user interface using modern web technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) integrated with open NASA APIs and datasets.

Creativity & Design Considerations:

What makes our project innovative is its focus on accessibility and simplicity—
dataRefs: NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) - Moving Object Search Tool (MOST): Used for determining orbital paths and fetching metadata for solar system objects (e.g., Asteroid 12 Victoria and 99942 Apophis).
NASA SPHEREx Mission Data (via IRSA): Referenced for spectral imaging datasets and all-sky spectral data releases.
